A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGGT-based semantic matching framework, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 includes Appendix A.1–A.9; v2 ends after the references and contains no appendix. The omissions and substantial presentation changes can be reliably compared.

before.justification: V1 reports original matching experiments, architectural and training ablations, per-category results, failure cases, and DINOv3 comparisons in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports original matching and ablation results, including additional symmetric-keypoint, reconstruction-fidelity, occlusion-detection, and confidence evaluations in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the frozen early VGGT blocks, fine-tuned semantic branch, DPT head predicting bidirectional grids and confidence, synthetic-data pipeline, four-stage training, and matching, reconstruction, uncertainty, and smoothness losses. V2 adds motivation but documents no changed method component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both use SPair-71k, AP-10k with intra-species, cross-species, and cross-family evaluation, and synthetic data derived from the same 18 categories. V2's symmetry, rotation, and confidence breakdowns examine correspondence and occlusion conditions already represented in v1; they do not establish additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds ASIC and supervised Geo-SC (S.) to Table 1's quantitative comparison, substantially strengthening the comparator set. V1's Geo-SC score row survives as Geo-SC (Flip), and DistillDIFT (W.S.) becomes DistillDIFT (S.). Conversely, the DINOv3 variants compared against the proposed method in v1 Appendix A.9 and Figure 29 are omitted.

E3.justification: V2 Section 4.2 changes the stated PCK normalization from image dimensions to object bounding-box dimensions and describes synthetic error as mean rather than summed squared error. It also introduces symmetric-keypoint aggregation, DINO/SD feature errors, FID, reconstruction PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, rotation-stratified occlusion AUC, and confidence-binned matching error. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative analyses of symmetric-keypoint ambiguity and invisibility across rotation angles and confidence bins. The main training and backbone ablation questions remain, but v1's additional qualitative ablations, explicit failure-case analysis, and DINOv3 model-size/pretraining comparisons are removed with the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, statistical confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 Table 2's 'confidence intervals' are bins of predicted pixel confidence, not statistical uncertainty estimates; their evaluation changes analyses and results rather than uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed method's SPair-71k PCK values 76.8/57.2/14.5 with 84.2/76.3/25.9, and many ablation values also change. These are revised reports rather than established same-protocol gains because metric definitions change. V2 adds extensive geometry, fidelity, and invisibility results, including mean AUC 0.92, while removing v1's per-category table and DINOv3 findings.

T1.justification: The method's mathematical equations remain equivalent apart from numbering and presentation. A limited definition change occurs in PCK's acceptance radius R = alpha max(H, W): H and W refer to image dimensions in v1 but object bounding-box dimensions in v2. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains VGGT-based dense matching with cycle consistency and synthetic-to-real training. V2 broadens the explicit novelty claim from the first adaptation of VGGT to the first feed-forward framework unifying 3D-aware descriptors and holistic dense matching, while presenting the existing requirements as a geometry-grounded matching task.

C2.justification: V2 adds a canonical-space explanation for transferring VGGT, a keypoint-overfitting interpretation, and a stronger interpretation of confidence/error correlation as identifying occlusions. It removes v1's substantive limitations concerning intricate structures, extreme non-rigid poses, and correspondence reversal on symmetric objects, together with the DINOv3 scaling discussion. The retained general future-work paragraph does not preserve these specific qualifications.

D1.justification: Removing Appendix A eliminates the Adam learning rate, numerical loss weights, synthetic-to-real training ratio, stage-specific training times, ablation budgets, and baseline implementation/project information. Architecture details and the five-day A6000 training statement remain. V2 newly states which baselines share the training dataset and that DistillDIFT uses more synthetic data, but overall reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced.

R1.justification: Most related-work coverage remains. V2 adds Qian et al.'s 'Bridging Viewpoint Gaps' and removes citations associated with omitted discussions, including CoTracker and DINOv3. Positioning emphasizes native 3D priors and the broader feed-forward novelty claim, but the underlying contrast with 2D-feature matching already appears in v1.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and affiliations, substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution statement, and conclusion, and expands the methodological motivation. Experimental settings, matching evaluation, and ablations become separate major sections; an acknowledgment is added and the entire appendix structure is removed.

P2.justification: V2 retypesets the paper, redraws and annotates Figure 1, reassembles Figure 3 using selected existing examples, and rearranges the confidence visualization. Table 1 gains substantial new structure, a new invisibility table is introduced, and the training ablation table is transposed. Most appendix displays disappear, although some examples are incorporated into the revised main figures.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens quantitative scrutiny of geometry, manifold preservation, and invisibility, and adds important comparators in Tables 1–2. However, it removes essential optimization and ablation details and the explicit failure analysis from v1's appendix. Large score revisions also accompany changed metric definitions without an explanation connecting the reports. The gains in empirical assessment and losses in reproducibility and qualification are substantial, leaving the overall net quality direction uncertain.
